writeup.headline: Zscaler rates Hold: strong growth and net cash balanced by high absolute valuation and negative operating margin.
writeup.thesis: Zscaler scores 58, a Hold, 7 points short of Buy. Growth is the main support, with TTM revenue growth of 25.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 24.9% year on year, though growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 100 thanks to net cash and cash at 2.05 times debt, and the FCF margin is 25.4%. Quality scores only 50, because the operating margin is -4.0%, stock-based compensation equals 24.5% of revenue, and the diluted share count is up 3.8% year on year. Valuation scores 30: in absolute terms the multiples are high, with P/S of 12.4x, P/FCF of 48.9x and an FCF yield 2.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is cheap overall (EV/EBIT not comparable), with P/S cheaper than at 48 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: High absolute valuation (12.4x sales, 48.9x FCF) leaves little room for a growth miss.
GAAP operating losses (-4.0% margin) and stock-based compensation at 24.5% of revenue dilute shareholders, with share count up 3.8% year on year.
Growth is slowing slightly, down 0.6 pp from the previous quarter.
The shares are volatile: down 39.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, yet now 26.8% above the 50-day average and 23.9% below the 52-week high, so a sharp rebound could reverse.
An existing securities investigation tied to the May 2026 stock drop remains in the background.
what_would_change: A 7-point rise in the composite score would reach Buy, for example through reaccelerating growth or a move to positive GAAP operating margin lifting the quality score.
A lower share price or stronger free cash flow would improve the valuation score of 30.
A fall of 14 points would mean Sell, which could follow a growth slowdown, a guidance cut, or a reversal of the strong recent price trend.
